targeting.title: Unexpected Token '<' in JSON: Fix Fetch Returning HTML
targeting.metaTitle: Unexpected Token '<' in JSON: Fix Fetch HTML
targeting.metaDescription: Fix unexpected token '<' in JSON by checking HTML responses, login redirects, API routes and empty bodies. Includes tested Fetch, Next.js and Vite examples.
targeting.excerpt: Find why an API returned HTML instead of JSON. Diagnose wrong routes, login redirects, frontend fallbacks and empty responses with tested JavaScript examples and focused Next.js and Vite fixes.
targeting.keywords: unexpected token html is not valid json, unexpected token in json at position 0, fetch returns html instead of json, api returns html instead of json, nextjs api returns html, response json unexpected end of json input
targeting.summary: Inspect the response URL, HTTP status, media type and body before changing the JSON parser; an HTML login or error page is not API data.|Use the eight-case reproduction and checked JSON reader to distinguish HTML, HTTP errors, empty responses and consumed streams.|Fix API routing or authentication at the source, preserve access controls, and verify the same request in the environment that failed.

competitorAndCaseReview.differentiation: Keep the actual response intact, give executable scenarios and compare successful HTML, valid error JSON, false MIME labels, body consumption and no-content responses.

competitorAndCaseReview.differentiation: Explain self-fetching using current official Next.js guidance; do not copy old caching advice or claim converting to a Client Component is a universal fix.

competitorAndCaseReview.limitation: Search result observed, but page content extraction failed. No claims attributed to its unseen answers.
